facts: A15 installs only pacman-owned immutable files under /usr; package removal has no hook that deletes XDG profile data or secret-provider entries.
The package desktop entry registers x-scheme-handler/p2pkanban and delegates the URI argument to the A13 bounded native deep-link parser.

Release preparation creates a deterministic source archive, injects the canonical UTS Cargo.lock, resolves an exact source checksum in the staged PKGBUILD, and records Cargo/npm/migration/protocol digests.
PKGBUILD prepare fetches the locked Cargo graph while build/check use Cargo --frozen; the application package has no self-updater or pacman/sudo invocation.
Signed-repository staging uses an external GPG fingerprint/agent to sign both package and repository database and records only public fingerprint plus artifact hashes.
inferences: Binding the UTS-accepted Cargo.lock into retained release source is safer than generating a floating Rust graph inside the package build, even though repository ownership of Cargo.lock remains explicit debt.
Keeping signing outside the build recipe prevents package construction from becoming a secret-bearing or privileged operation.
proposals: Promote a host-proven Cargo.lock into repository ownership in a later bounded correction so arbitrary source checkouts can reproduce the same Rust graph without first running UTS.
Replace the packaging-only license notice with the project owner approved software license before any public AUR or public-mirror publication.

unresolved: Clean-chroot package build, namcap on the produced package, pacman -Qkk/install/remove preservation and real release-key repository publication require Arch host/manual evidence.
Exact direct runtime dependencies should be refined from package namcap/ldd evidence after the first clean-chroot artifact rather than guessed from transitive desktop packages.
